To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified a set of 39 constructs from published implementation theory that we consolidated into a framework for implementation research.

we developed a new theory, the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFiR), that is a synthesis of existing theories and that includes constructs related to the intervention, outer setting, and inner setting, characteristics related to individuals involved, and processes of implementation.

the CFIR provides a comprehensive and pragmatic structure to guide implementation research, including formative evaluations of implementation strategies, and to build an implementation knowledge base across settings and studies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the CFIR as a conceptual model that can be used to help guide and evaluate implementation of evidence-based interventions.
the development of a framework that can be used to help guide implementation science research and practice in the real world.
the translation of research into practice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CFIR offers an overarching typological framework for advancing implementation theory development and testing.
the CFIR provides a comprehensive and detailed framework for advancing implementation research.
the CFIR is an important contribution to the implementation science literature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are proposing a framework that is comprehensive, parsimonious, and practical.
the CFIR can serve as a framework to guide future implementation research, and it is a resource for implementation science researchers to use in their own studies.

the CFIR provides a framework that can help to advance the science of implementation by helping researchers and practitioners to better understand and measure implementation constructs, identify gaps in knowledge, and guide the development of theory based interventions and implementation strategies.
The main takeaway from our work is that

there are a number of constructs that have been found to be important in implementation, and we need to be more systematic about how they are defined, how they are measured, and how they are related to one another.
implementation science needs to move from a focus on what works in a specific setting to a focus on what is likely to work in any setting.
the CFIR is not a theory in itself, but rather a framework for organizing and integrating multiple theories and constructs.
